java.say: At start-up, the program makes the real rate source and gives it to the calculator.
The calculator keeps the source in a field. It only knows it as RateSource, the interface. This is constructor injection.
Later, price() asks its source for the rate. It does not know whether a database is behind it.
In the application, the source asks the database. In a test, another RateSource can take its place.
